problem: Using the method of orthogonal transformations, find the canonical form of $Q(x)={x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2}+4{x}_{1}{x}_{3}.$

activity_context.topic_title: Finding the Canonical Form of a Quadratic Form Using Orthogonal Transformations

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Canonical Form of a Quadratic Function by Finding Eigenvalues
examples.problem: Using the method of orthogonal transformations, find the canonical form of $Q(\mathbf{x})=x_1^2+x_2^2+2x_3^2+4x_1x_2.$
examples.worked_solution:
First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14076285/assets/44753acffd8b6384cd291f9b0758edd7676acb319caa22d5b07be36dcf72a5a6.png)

Every quadratic form can be reduced to its canonical (diagonal) form using orthogonal transformations.

To find the coefficients of the canonical form, we need to calculate the eigenvalues of $A\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}|A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & 1-\lambda  & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (2-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & 2 \\ 2 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (2-\lambda )((1-\lambda )(1-\lambda )-4) & =0 \\ (2-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-2\lambda -3) & =0 \\ (2-\lambda )(\lambda -3)(\lambda +1) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =3,\,2,\,-1\end{aligned}
$$

 

So, writing the eigenvalues in descending order, we obtain the diagonal matrix

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14076285/assets/217b5d7d3b82800bdfc44d83ca8b068e02a37759e52b7a8382505bfb102f753f.png)

The corresponding quadratic form after a change of variables is

$$
3y_1^2 + 2y_2^2 - y_3^2.
$$
